937721e208d5fe04e611: Grand Line Chronicles · Guidelines for Mechanical Body and Modules
7b6a4f0482abfc0f9024: A Cyborg does not simply carry tools: they integrate them into their body. Mechanical Body establishes how many Modules it can house and what technological level it can support; Modules define what that technology can do.
6dcc39965736ad2d6b89: This manual gathers the rules needed to design clear, comparable Modules that can be used at the table, without turning every technological description into an unlimited collection of bonuses.
3f3ccfd0bdfa4c4af977: A Cyborg is an individual whose body has been modified through prosthetics, implants and integrated mechanical devices. Two Cyborgs of the same Grade can have completely different bodies: one could be a weapons platform, while another focuses on mobility, sensors or tools.
279446ed3b55b20953f5: Every Cyborg possesses the Racial Technique Mechanical Body. Its Grade represents the quality and level of integration of the technology in the body, not the character's amount of metal or mass.
6418597a6e87d4b1e0e2: Mechanical Body determines two things: the number of available slots and the maximum Technology Tier of installable Modules.
bf221841e9e84518f5b0: A Module is a technological device integrated into the body and recorded as part of Mechanical Body. It can be an artificial limb, a weapon, a thruster, armour, a sensor, a tool or another consistent system.
91e2eafaeeea4beca938: Every Module must have a concrete function. Calling a device “advanced” grants no benefits: what it is designed to do must be defined.
b898f901d039c5f09a55: A Module is not a Technique. The Module is the device; the Technique is the particular way the character uses their abilities.
1fa1f8b2f8fe6e3d570e: A Module can be used according to its function or as the means of executing a compatible Technique. It does not automatically grant Signature Move Builder Effects, roll bonuses, Statuses, additional damage or other properties not specified in its sheet.
8250b2be3a14a12e92a4: The function states what a Module can do; the Technology Tier establishes how much it can do. Special Effects introduce any exceptions. Slots, energy, activation and integrity establish when the device can be used.
36796fcd6afc17ef3fe9: The narrative description cannot freely increase power, distance or autonomy. At the same time, the rules define limits and values without imposing the same arsenal on every Cyborg.
9c9ef2ec2d24469bcd82: Mechanical Body measures the Cyborg's level of technological integration. Its ordinary progression is d6 → d8 → d10 → d12 → d20 and it has no Prestige progression.
8d690a5834d15ead7c0e: A Cyborg can install Modules of their own Technology Tier or a lower Tier. Having a free slot does not allow a device beyond their Mechanical Body Grade to be installed.
c9b96027bc814cd3571d: Slots measure how many Modules can be integrated; Technology Tier measures how advanced each Module can be.
42acd8e58c1fe9c32b41: Every installed Module normally occupies 1 slot, regardless of Tier.
4cdf129a45d71fbd2cc3: A slot does not necessarily correspond to an anatomical part. Multiple Modules can occupy the same part of the body if the configuration is plausible, but independent technological systems remain separate Modules.
4afbefd10c027f3ccce2: Technology Tier indicates the Mechanical Body requirement. Weapon Grade instead indicates the die used by a Weapon Module. The two values are separate: a Tier d10 cannon could, for example, be a d8 weapon.
2401ab914672eecedf52: When Mechanical Body increases in Grade, the Cyborg gains the new slot specified by the table and can install Modules of the new Tier. They do not receive a new Module for free.
75370df36d1214f47716: Modules already owned do not automatically increase in Tier. To improve them, they must be modified, rebuilt or replaced through the specified procedures.
748e6c9750ba72852fd6: Mechanical Body is independent of the Strength Attribute. Increasing Mechanical Body does not increase Strength, Passive Defence, unarmed damage or general lifting capacity. Increasing Strength does not grant slots or access to higher Tiers.
a20247b4d7c0da226675: The ordinary limit is d20: 5 slots and Modules up to Tier d20. Any exceptions must come from a specific ability.
3b90ce8869a5170debe5: Every Module uses a standard sheet. The sheet separates function, operational state, any Special Effects and resources, so what the device can do is always clear.
653890d4d56b5ca46f00: Only if the Module can be used as a weapon.
6b97e2736a89bcc35f52: What the device is built to do.
fecb28fb4a4ff219c68c: What the Module can do when operational.
db1eaf999561beadf8ca: Any limitations on use as the means of execution.
a1590c4b76ba1bde5885: A Module can exist without being installed. Only an installed Module occupies a slot and becomes part of the Mechanical Body system.
32c8920f0291b46f7ee7: An Intact Module is functional; a Damaged Module cannot use its Operational Function, Special Effect or Techniques that require it until repaired.
34adfec37dfe8d6a91bf: An installed, intact Module can be Active or Inactive. Being installed, being intact and being active are three distinct conditions.
9cc1582c90b50f43d934: The Inactive function includes only physical properties not requiring the system's operational functioning: for example, a compartment that continues to hold objects or an artificial limb retaining normal mobility if the design provides for it.
7ffdcc04fefd2c5354ac: Propulsion, advanced sensors, defensive bonuses, Special Effects and linked Techniques do not automatically remain active. If the sheet specifies no Inactive function, an inactive Module grants no mechanical benefits.
471ac5c6639a7161b71c: The Active function instead describes the device's normal functioning when installed, intact and active.
f34361757ef0aa32163c: A Module can have at most one Special Effect. If it uses a dedicated resource, the sheet specifies capacity, consumption and recharging. Compatible Techniques and Limits specify any further conditions without granting additional benefits.
e6f3fef407b88106445e: Technology Tier establishes the maximum limit of the Module's Main Function. It does not automatically grant every capability in the same row: each device uses only the parameters needed for its function.
d8eaa84be54e906680ca: Functional reach indicates how far a device can act physically; Displacement indicates the distance generated by a Mobility Function; Mechanical strength indicates the ordinary operating load; Sensors and Functional area indicate their respective maximum radii.
03636091914beea9764a: Assisted thrust: acceleration, jumps, braking and corrections. No continuous flight.
d4d902402beb2841f25d: Brief aerial Displacement: can lift off, but must finish on a surface.
0cb643a7c36fe5152c78: Flight: three-dimensional movement and staying airborne while the system is operational.
84d329d54a15a0de63b1: Advanced flight: stable control in complex manoeuvres and ordinary difficult conditions.
a1f090c4439d77a711be: Legendary flight: maximum ordinary technological control, always within distance and energy limits.
42a8b24210b6c05ff64e: Part of the body or a limited direction
97bd673334ba8b2cafab: User + 1 adjacent target or a small barrier
4cef024f2f3d46733244: The Tier establishes the scale of protection, not the damage cancelled: the specific benefit depends on the chosen Defensive Function.
51578fc52e2301fa0ecd: The tables represent normal operating conditions. Temporarily exceeding a load or operating in extreme conditions may require an appropriate Check, but does not permanently turn a Module into a higher Tier.
988b7ffb4723773d6eea: No Tier automatically grants Builder effects such as Grapple, Launch, Statuses, Areas, Ranges or other combat results. Tier describes only the device's material capability. Combat effects come from specific Functions, Special Effects, Weapon Modules, Techniques or Talents. Areas and Persistent Zones require a function or design expressly producing them. The ordinary Builder no longer grants additional damage dice as a purchasable effect.
97370f936fe9c3391d02: A Module has one Main Function. Secondary components necessary for it to function are allowed, but independent mechanical abilities require a compatible Special Effect or a second Module.
6acee84483020aae9328: The Main Function is what the Module can normally do. A continuous Function operates while the Module is active; an operational Function normally requires 1 Action unless its description states otherwise.
ab9304c02bf5e8cdb34e: A Module directly dealing damage must be a Weapon Module or use a Technique or ability expressly assigning damage or Statuses.
d93da284d4ca129b9195: A Weapon Module states whether it is Melee or Ranged and has a Weapon Grade. Technology Tier establishes whether the body can support it; Weapon Grade determines its offensive effectiveness.
cfb0469a3d43ce0dc37e: The two main Defensive Functions are Armour and Shield/Barrier.
e5639f0658d74b4a13a6: Reduction applies after any halving and cannot take damage below 0. Specific resistances to fire, cold, electricity, acid, poison, Haki or other damage require a property provided by the design.
ce077c767aa0c93b8ff8: When correctly facing the threat, grants Partial Cover: PD +2. Tier increases the protected scale, not the bonus.
adb528c62642862bfc46: User + up to 3 allies within 3 m
4693e217bca3671b9d2f: Partial Cover does not stack with another identical source; the best benefit is used. Full Cover requires a specific ability.
bf0d2b2091c896f6ce49: A Thruster uses the Displacement of its Tier once per turn. This Displacement adds to normal Movement and does not constitute an additional Action. Available flight capabilities depend on Tier according to Chapter 4. Any energy consumption is paid normally.
f136b6ba1f06a1177051: Manipulators, cables, harpoons and similar systems use their Tier's Functional reach and Mechanical strength to grasp, support, move or operate objects.
7d19323e686e33b773fc: Against a creature, physically reaching it does not automatically grant Grapple, Immobilised, Attraction, Launch or other forced displacement. These results require a normal appropriate check, a Technique with an effect compatible with its Style, or a Module Function or Special Effect expressly granting them.
b20a377921b9c0fe9287: An anchoring system can support the Cyborg, pull objects within its load capacity or allow an anchored point to be reached, always within the device's Reach.
b5465c0d96014e108a7f: Utility Modules include sensors, integrated tools, and analysis, communication, lighting and storage systems.
0023678841b2a97e0e1f: A Sensor is designed for a defined type of information and uses the radius specified by its Tier. It does not automatically detect everything within that radius: concealment, interference and environmental conditions may require a Check.
bc18a98db018f4894fd6: Mobile laboratory specialising in a single field
59cf753e093ac619e197: An Integrated tool replaces the necessary equipment, but does not automatically increase the Skill, provide materials or grant professional Talents.
aef9ce739150284fa5aa: A Module can emit light, smoke, foam, steam, signals, liquids or other elements within its Tier's Functional area. Emission alone does not automatically inflict damage, Statuses, Advantage or Disadvantage: a rule granting a combat effect is needed to obtain one.
dfbf41287003cce3cfc5: A player can propose creative uses consistent with the Function. The GM can permit them directly or require a Check. Creative use does not turn the Module into a Function it does not possess or automatically duplicate effects already supplied by Techniques or Special Effects.
7793927891671b801aff: A Special Effect is an additional property of the Module. It is optional, and each Module can have at most one. A single Effect grants only one main mechanical benefit: conditions and limits can specify it, but cannot conceal multiple independent advantages.
4b4f58740a48181ed62c: The Special Effect belongs to the same Technology Tier as the Module and must be consistent with its functioning.
700ba0652389e4903e09: Reduces the cost of a specific ability used through the Module. It must precisely identify the Technique, Builder Effect or ability concerned.
40d277bfbcf51556d8fd: 1 Discount Point = −1 ST. The cost cannot fall below 1 ST.
a7eda630cbf3b4046e57: From d8: 2 Discount Points = −1 Effect Slot. A Slot can decrease to 0.
1139d903d835c8e40155: The Discount does not grant the ability, remove requirements or apply outside the Module.
c6dc3482bb1a7c0c821e: Multiple Discounts on the same cost do not automatically stack: use the best.
083917beb93b2348331f: Makes one Signature Move Builder Effect materially enabled by the technology available through the Module.
f290d99df7ea0584c864: The unlocked Effect cannot have a minimum Grade above the Module's Tier. Unlock does not reduce the minimum Grade or remove Form, Slots, ST, Talent prerequisites, Haki, Fruits, Ultimate, Prestige or fundamental limits of the Role Manuals.
0516c42f144daf0ff395: A Passive works while the Module is installed, intact and active. The main models are:
cf7b3c3cf38e8d5b2966: Improves one parameter of the Main Function.
91ffa5e1ba06c978e980: Advantage on a very specific type of Check linked to the Function.
ddb2da24706495c6e0f0: Ignores a specific operational penalty hindering the Function.
eb28a3a89b0a95187cae: Protects the Function against a very specific category of interference.
5ea11fb4a2e351faf623: Maximum expression of one of the previous models, without immunities or extra actions.
c887f870542dbaf3d33b: For Optimisation, the maximum increase of the chosen parameter is:
d539922eb51e4b070455: Allows a Module property to be used in response to a specific Trigger. The sheet must state the Trigger, effect, frequency and any costs. The Reaction does not grant additional Reactions.
402b84ec302d441edfa3: The Reaction uses only one Module Function and normally pays Energy, Charges, ST or Ammunition. From d12, it can use a Function that would normally require an Action, provided the Trigger is specific. At d20, it can include the Module's Emergency Activation as part of the same Reaction.
4a41288b6e20eb9e24fe: A Curse expands a Discount, Unlock, Passive or Reaction in only one aspect, but imposes a real mechanical consequence. It can represent overload, instability, overheating or experimental technology.
aafd6fd66629844c31b2: Discount: can extend to a small, consistent family of effects.
0c46497550f04eeb6b13: Unlock: can include 2 closely linked Effects.
1c77c8c5738e494da25f: Passive: can extend the benefit to two closely related conditions.
047448e2770d0a3acd02: Reaction: can increase by 1 use per combat, without exceeding the normal Reaction economy.
0f7b51401164cb7193fc: Overheating: the Module becomes Inactive until the start of the next turn.
cf6a224b5c68f8e64e1d: The consequence must be truly relevant. A Curse does not allow Tier d20 to be exceeded.
acf32f89ea6903bf2058: Unless explicitly excepted, a Special Effect requires the Module to be Installed, Intact and Active.
096da1a24be725a93919: If it modifies a Technique, the Technique must be executed through that Module.
a849199b6b086518967b: Identical effects do not automatically multiply: two sources of Advantage remain a single Advantage; two identical Unlocks give no further benefits.
07384a97a0f966a3679d: No normal Special Effect grants additional Actions, additional Reactions, Ultimate, Haki, Prestige, Devil Fruits, Role Talents, general immunity or infinite resources.
f33aeded5dcc5b0a3b5a: Not all Modules require a separate resource. Each sheet specifies Energy: None or a consistent source such as a battery, fuel, pressure, ammunition or other Charges. Energy limits uses that actually require it, not every normal movement of the device.
a280c21be7ae5ad8fae6: A normal use consumes 1 Charge. Particularly intense Functions can specify higher consumption or an upkeep cost; consumption must appear in the sheet.
2de44b6eef5a1fd2fb51: Charges and Stamina are different resources. If a Technique costs ST and the Module executing it consumes Charges, both are paid. Charges do not replace the Technique's cost.
a6766808e3ccd83fc648: Charges are not automatically recovered through Rest. If the necessary resource is available, a normal full recharge requires 10 minutes outside combat. Ammunition, special fuels or rare resources must be owned, purchased or produced according to the design.
8f2b50e053164fef8ae1: An easy-to-find source does not make the Module infinite. A 5-Charge tank remains a 5-Charge tank even if it uses water, air, coal or electricity and the source is immediately available.
43c6fc087f67d34cc795: A Module with Energy: None can normally use its Function. Actions, ST, limits, activation and any Special Effects specified by the sheet still apply.
8c8bd98943039ca1e917: A Module built to deal damage directly can be classified as a Weapon Module and has both a Technology Tier and a Weapon Grade.
468c79a17fd3fc4fe29c: Weapon Grade follows the scale d4 → d6 → d8 → d10 → d12 → d20 and cannot exceed the Module's Technology Tier.
67a2dea4c808294a4abe: Example: d10 Module · d8 Weapon is valid; d8 Module · d10 Weapon is not.
75826d847e85026663e2: When a Weapon Module makes a normal attack, it uses:
67efb12d62059acb0dad: Range, ammunition and special conditions depend on the design or Catalogue entry.
aa1d96abc3882f245e51: A Module can execute a compatible Technique, but does not replace the Technique Die. The Technique normally uses Attribute + Technique Die and its own Damage Die. The Module provides the physical means, its Function, any Special Effect and any Charge costs.
c7ff1fa13b306678d82b: The Technique's Grade still depends on the Attribute used and does not increase because the Module has a higher Tier. The Technique must also be physically compatible with the device and meet Form, Slots, ST, requirements and any Role limitations.
ecc389a4398dbe2bf36d: When a Technique uses a property already made possible by the Module, that property is the means of the action and is not applied twice. A telescopic arm allowing a target to be reached does not add a second Attraction to a Technique that already has Attraction.
e46a57ddd19427592971: The Cyborg can have multiple Modules installed, but normally keeps only one Active Module at a time.
7ad741c1f60a04f6955b: The Active Module can use its Active function, Special Effect and linked Techniques. The other installed Modules remain Inactive and retain only any Inactive functions specified in their sheets.
ac105fe925860e9cf057: Outside combat, the Cyborg freely chooses which Module to keep active. At the start of a battle they retain the one already active; if none was declared, they choose one without spending Actions.
93c679840e4d15225e43: Once during their turn, the Cyborg can switch their Active Module for free. Switching uses no Action, Bonus Action, Movement or Reaction.
c768319f45389561dafb: The new Module immediately becomes Active and the previous one Inactive. A second free switch in the same turn is not possible.
f9419c19ec726ab56199: A Module remains Active until replaced, voluntarily shut down, Damaged, deprived of its necessary resource or deactivated by a specific ability. It does not automatically shut down at the end of a turn or battle.
e5689e6dcbc884b50983: Voluntarily shutting down a Module during your turn is free, but does not grant a second switch in the same turn.
1281d2ef863485d551e9: Normally, you cannot switch Modules outside your turn. An Effect or ability with Emergency Activation can do so through a Reaction; the new Module immediately replaces the previous one.
e22677448c4f7191c6b1: A Module can be built by the crew, commissioned from a professional or obtained during the adventure. Technology Tier determines its construction difficulty; function, materials and appearance remain linked to the individual design.
2f4849d3a02ebcbae0d3: Construction normally uses Cunning + Mechanics. The Module's Tier establishes the minimum Mechanics Grade, Threshold and base work time.
04157021626d9c95d9c4: The Mechanics requirement indicates the minimum proficiency needed to attempt the design. Engineer Talents can normally modify time, materials, results or other conditions when their descriptions allow it.
d5ce447cc4c6ce56aff9: The table provides reference values. A particularly simple, bulky, experimental or unconventional design can be modified by the GM without changing the Module's Technology Tier.
755ace4ce23f28e7b40a: There is no universal list of mandatory materials for each Tier. Materials vary by Module and are chosen by the GM based on what the device must actually do.
efdbdd6172d3bc6ef00c: The GM has full creative freedom to decide components, quantities, availability and origin: they can be purchased, salvaged from machinery, obtained as a reward or become the objective of a search during the adventure.
03ee9f66452bbb4042cc: The indicative value given in the table serves only as an economic reference. It is not a shopping list or a mandatory cost. If the crew already owns some components, they do not have to pay for them again; if the design requires rare or unique materials, the GM can increase their value or require them to be obtained narratively.
d4a027e68a6450142ad8: A rare material does not automatically make the Module more powerful: mechanical values still depend on Tier, Function and any Special Effect.
70535f2338f89635a2d1: A Cyborg can entrust construction to a Mechanic or external workshop. The price in the External professional column normally includes labour, ordinary materials and installation.
12d52afa2e3ff2a6d3b6: Exceptional materials, unique components or technologies requiring a specific adventure are not automatically included in the price. A professional capable of building d12 or d20 Modules is not guaranteed merely by possessing Berry and remains the GM's choice.
9871b8a7d864bc8ea46c: When the work is commissioned, the player does not make the construction Check: the hired professional is assumed to have the required proficiency.
